10845.author: ghyls
10845.body:
The flag `--with-rocm=$ROCM_HIP_ROOT` we had in `ucx.spec` does not seem to be enough to make the `rocm` transports available to UCX (see [1]). This prevents UCX from knowing about AMD GPU pointers which prevents us from using it to do RDMA with AMD GPUs.

In this case, the `./configure` command would print

```
checking for hsa.h... no
configure: WARNING: ROCm not found
```

which is very easy to miss.


This PR 
- Adds the Include and Library flags that UCX needs to build the rocm UCT and UCM modules 
- Adds a quick test to check for the generated rocm modules. This is just to allow us to realize if this gets broken in future UCX version upgrades, etc.


---
[1]

The rocm support can be checked with `ucx_info -b`.

Before this PR

```
[...]
#define UCX_MODULE_SUBDIR         "ucx"
#define VERSION                   "1.21"
#define restrict                  __restrict__
#define test_MODULES              ":module"
#define ucm_MODULES               ":cuda"
#define ucs_MODULES               ""
#define uct_MODULES               ":cuda:ib:rdmacm:cma:xpmem"
#define uct_cuda_MODULES          ":gdrcopy"
#define uct_ib_MODULES            ":mlx5:efa"
#define uct_ib_mlx5_MODULES       ":gda"
#define uct_rocm_MODULES          ""
#define ucx_perftest_MODULES      ":cuda"
```

And after

```
#define UCX_MODULE_SUBDIR         "ucx"
#define VERSION                   "1.21"
#define restrict                  __restrict__
#define test_MODULES              ":module"
#define ucm_MODULES               ":cuda:rocm"
#define ucs_MODULES               ""
#define uct_MODULES               ":cuda:ib:rdmacm:rocm:cma:xpmem"
#define uct_cuda_MODULES          ":gdrcopy"
#define uct_ib_MODULES            ":mlx5:efa"
#define uct_ib_mlx5_MODULES       ":gda"
#define uct_rocm_MODULES          ""
#define ucx_perftest_MODULES      ":cuda:rocm:mad"
```




@fwyzard FYI
10845.title: Extend rocm support in ucx

10884.author: fwyzard
10884.body:
MIGraphX's TensorFlow parser compiles its own copy of the TensorFlow protobuf messages, in the "tensorflow" package, and links them against the shared protobuf library. Loading it together with CMSSW's TensorFlow registers the same messages twice in the global descriptor pool, and protobuf aborts the process.

See ROCm/AMDMIGraphX#5089 and ROCm/AMDMIGraphX#5332 for more information, and ROCm/AMDMIGraphX#5333 for the upstream fix.
10884.title: MIGraphX: give the TF protobuf messages and files unique names

49003.author: Jared-Fraticelli
49003.body:
#### PR description:

The TkTriplet word is updated to contain a valid bit, triplet pT, eta, and phi fields (which are currently set to 0), a triplet invariant mass field, the three triplet track pTs,  and an unassigned field. The new word spans 97 bits, and is padded with zeroes to span 128 bits (evenly spanning two 64-bit link data words). The tktriplet emulation plugin finds the three highest pT tracks in an event, computes the invariant mass from them, and fills the output word with the aforementioned nonzero fields.

https://indico.cern.ch/event/1588031/
- See the above indico page for a talk regarding the W->3pi updates 

#### PR validation:

Tests have been done to ensure that the output tktriplet word is correctly written in APX board format. The word currently spans the first two 64-bit link words of each event on link 2, and tests using HLS firmware have shown that the invariant mass and triplet track pT fields can be correctly decoded from the test vectors.

51795.author: ghyls
51795.body:
#### PR description:

Products without a TrivialSerialisation plugin cannot be trivially serialised. If "persistent=false" is also set for these products in the corresponding `classes_def.xml`, these products cannot be serialised through ROOT either. Products that satisfy these two conditions have no serialisation mechanism, and thus cannot be transferred by the MPI modules.

These conditions are already being checked by the `MPISenderPortable.cc` and `MPIReceiverPortable.cc` modules, but a unit test is currently missing for this check.

This PR introduces the test. The test attempts to transfer a `MPIToken`, which satisfies these two conditions and for which there is no serialisation mechanism. A `cmsRun` job is then launched, and the test looks for the expected error in the output. If the expected exception is thrown, the test passes. Otherwise it fails.

#### PR validation:

The test triggers the expected CMSSW exception and passes.
51795.title: Add a unit test to check the handling of transient products in MPI modules

51892.author: ghyls
51892.body:
#### PR description:

Add a `DumpDependencyGraph` service, which dumps the module dependencies of a process as `.json`. This `.json` can then be parsed by other modules.


A use case will be the part of the `HeterogeneousCore/MPICore` package that, from a single-process CMSSW configuration, generates a client and a server-side configurations. This operation requires as input the list of modules intended to be offloaded to the server process. The `DumpDependencyGraph` service is used to understand which products need to be sent forth and back between the client and the server, and how `EDFilters` should be placed in the server configuration so that offloaded modules run only when needed. The changes in `HeterogeneousCore/MPICore` will come later as a separate PR.


#### PR validation:

A test has been added consisting on three files:

`FWCore/Services/test/test_dumpDependencyGraph_cfg.py`
- Defines the initial CMSSW configuration that will be taken as input by `DumpDependencyGraph`

`FWCore/Services/test/test_dumpDependencyGraph_check.py`
- A python script that will parse the generated `.json`, and check that its contents match what `test_dumpDependencyGraph_cfg.py` declared.

`FWCore/Services/test/test_dumpDependencyGraph.sh`
- Run `cmsRun test_dumpDependencyGraph_cfg.py`, then run `python3 test_dumpDependencyGraph_check.py`. `exit 0` if both commands succeeded, fail otherwise.
51892.title: Add a DumpDependencyGraph service to FWCore/Services

#### PR description:

Add a hook that allows a client of the Framework to add a customization point for the edm::Event::put and edm::Event::emplace functions. This allows modifying a product based on the ProductDescription and ProductID of the product. To use this, the function ```assigningProductTo``` should be defined in a header. Then to make use of the customization, a producer needs to include the header defining the function. The producer would need to do nothing else.

Currently, nothing in CMSSW uses this hook. Since nothing has implemented this function, the ```if constexpr``` in the code completely removes the added code at compilation. It should have no effect on existing CMSSW executables. The first user of this hook will be the Code4Hep project and that code is external to CMSSW (code4hep/Code4hep#35).

51954.author: Electricks94
51954.body:
#### PR description:

PR [#49995](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/49995?utm_source=gemini) introduced macros allowing custom methods to be inserted into View and ConstView classes, but this capability was strictly limited to SoABlocks layouts. This PR extends custom method support to standard SoA layouts and streamlines the SoABlocks backend so that it can use the methods macros with more parameters. This is needed because the columns macros of the standard SoA Layout class uses more parameters than the SoA_BLOCK macro. To solve this all downstram macros of the SoABlocks backend are simplified to not expand on all parameters but only on the ones that they actually need. This also simplifies the backend.

The idea of this PR was previously introduced by @leobeltra in [#48829](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/48829). In the original form SoABlocks did not exist, hence no unification needed to be done. The original PR has been closed because it was not clear at the time how functions are injected to run on heterogeneous hardware. In the meantime the backend converged to using the `SOA_HOST_DEVICE` for `SOA_ELEMENT_METHODS`, `SOA_CONST_ELEMENT_METHODS`, and for `SOA_VIEW_METHODS` and `SOA_CONST_VIEW_METHODS` used in SoABlocks. Hence, there is no reason anymore why the feature should not be used in the same way for Views of normal SoA Layouts. 

**Key Changes**

- Extended View Method Support: Standard SoA layouts can now define custom View and ConstView methods using the unified `SOA_VIEW_METHODS` and `SOA_CONST_VIEW_METHODS` macro.
- Backend Simplification: Downstream helper macros of the SoABlocks backend now explicitly extract only the parameters they actually consume, removing the legacy pattern where full, unneeded parameter tuples were blindly forwarded.

#### PR validation:

locally tested on unit test, purly technical PR

FYI: @felicepantaleo @sbaldu
51954.title: Implement View methods for SoA Layouts

52013.body:
#### PR description:

Cluster shape filter (`ClusterShapeHitFilter`) reads its pixel cut windows from text files shipped with CMSSW so changing them requires a new release. This PR adds a conditions payload for these pixel windows, so they can be changed via GTs.

Payload consists of any number of tables, each with one row per cluster size (`part dx dy` + 8 window limits, i.e. the `.par` columns without the unused density/points statistics), plus an ordered list of rules assigning BPIX layers / FPix disks to a table. This allows more flexibility than current implementation that only differentiates L1 / rest of BPIX / FPIX.

No change in output is expected: the record is not consumed yet. After this is in a release, the payloads will be uploaded and added to the GTs, and a follow-up PR will switch `ClusterShapeHitFilterESProducer` and `ClusterShapeHitFilter` from the files to the record.

52023.author: makortel
52023.body:
#### PR description:

Test failures in https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/51867#issuecomment-5876468346 showed that `L1MetPfProducer` used `edm::FileInPath` for an absolute path. Deeper look in the code showed a few additional problems
- mutable global state (via function-`static` variables)
- the path to the file to be read depending on the module construction order (via function call order dependency caused by the function-`static` variables)

These were fixed by refactoring the namespaces with free functions to classes, so that the full path is resolved once, and the JSON file is read upon construction (instead of lazy loading). This way each module's configuration fully dictates the JSON file(s) that module reads.

In addition, the type of the `JERFile` parameter of the `L1JUMPProducer` was changed from `string` to `FileInPath` to record the resolved location in the provenance.

Further issues on e.g. not conforming CMS' naming convention (https://cms-sw.github.io/cms_coding_rules.html) were not touched.

This refactoring was assisted with AI.

52053.author: fwyzard
52053.body:
#### PR description:

Pickle a python configuration, optionally compressing it with zlib or zstd. The pickled configuration can be written to a binary blob, or encoded with base64 into a self-contained python configuration.

By default the pickle is compressed with zstd (level 6) and encoded with base64 into a self-contained python configuration, written to standard output.
```
Usage: edmConfigPickle [-#] [-z | -s] [-b | -p] [-o FILE] config.py [args ...]

Positional arguments:
  config.py             python configuration file
  args ...              arguments passed to the python configuration file while
                        it is loaded (see below)

Options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -#                    compression level, between 1 and 9 for zlib and between
                        1 and 19 for zstd, or 0 to leave the pickle uncompressed
                        (default: 6)
  -z, --zlib            compress with zlib
  -s, --zstd            compress with zstd (default)
  -b, --base64          encode with base64 and write a self-contained python
                        configuration (default)
  -p, --pickle          write the (compressed) pickle as a binary file, without
                        base64 encoding
  -o, --output FILE     write the output to FILE instead of standard output; use
                        "-o -" to write a binary pickle to standard output

The arguments after config.py are passed to the configuration while it is loaded, as with
"cmsRun config.py args" or "edmConfigDump config.py args": their effect is stored in the
pickled configuration, and they are only recorded in a comment at the beginning of the
output. Any arguments given to cmsRun when running the pickled configuration are ignored:
to change them, run edmConfigPickle again with the new arguments.
```

#### PR validation:

The new unit tests pass.
52053.title: Implement `edmConfigPickle` and its unit test

52081.author: YonsiG
52081.body:
#### PR description:

In `HGCalRawToDigi::produce`, the three host SoA collections (`digis`, `econdPacketInfo`, `fedPacketInfo`) are allocated with a size taken from the module indexer, i.e. the maximum possible number of modules / channels / FEDs. The unpacker then fills only the rows that correspond to data actually present in the FED payload. Rows (and columns) it never writes keep whatever was left in the allocated memory, so the products contain non-deterministic, uninitialised values.

This PR zero-initialises the three collections right after allocation with `zeroInitialise()`.

Expected changes in the output:
- Entries written by the unpacker: unchanged.
- Entries not written by the unpacker: now always zero instead of leftover memory.
- As a consequence the output is reproducible from run to run, and it compresses much better, since the uninitialised entries were effectively random bytes.

#### PR validation:

Ran runTheMatrix workflow 77 on an HGCal test-beam sample ([N] events) three times before the fix and three times after it, writing the three SoA products with LZMA level 4:

- All entries written by the unpacker are identical before and after the fix; only the previously uninitialised entries changed (to zero).
- Before the fix the compressed size differs from run to run, showing the content was not reproducible. After the fix the three runs are identical.
- The uncompressed size is unchanged, as the buffer capacity is the same.

Compressed size per event (B/event, LZMA 4):

| Product | Uncompressed | Before fix (run 1 / 2 / 3) | After fix (runs 13) | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| SoA digis | 29,347 | 3,102 / 4,441 / 3,966 | 2,160 | 30% to 51% |
| FED packet info | 40,549 | 3,615 / 3,429 / 7,535 | 661 | 81% to 91% |
| ECON-D packet info | 3,676 | 590 / 566 / 771 | 496 | 12% to 36% |
| **Total** | **73,572** | **7,306 / 8,435 / 12,271** | **3,316** | **55% to 73%** |

`scram b`, `scram b code-checks` and `scram b code-format` pass.
52081.title: Zero initialization to hgcalDigis variables
